The RHEA powders with nominal composition of Ti62Nb12Mo12Ta12W2 (atom ratio) were prepared using MA method. The MA process was carried out using the planetary ball mill (MSK-SFM-I). High-purity (≥ 99.9 wt%) Ti (< 100 μm), Nb (< 100 μm), Mo (< 1 μm), Ta (< 5 μm) and W (< 1 μm) powders and the stainless-steel grinding ball were mixed and sealed in a stainless-steel grinding tank in a weight ratio of 10:1. The rotation speed was set as 300 r/min. The running time of a single round is 30 min, and an interval of 15 min was added between two adjacent rounds. The total effective milling time is 50 h, and the alloyed RHEA powder after milling was collected. To prevent the oxidation of powder, powder loading and extraction processes were completed in Argon atmosphere.

Then, the alloyed powder was loaded into a high-strength graphite mold with an inner diameter of 20 mm and held at 1550–1700 °C for 10 min under an axial pressure of 50 MPa. The sintering process was conducted using SPS-20T-10-III system

Due to the thermal activation conditions provided by high temperature, the dynamic recovery phenomenon appears which offsets the work hardening.
For Ti62Nb12Mo12Ta12W2 alloy, the solid solution strengthening effect plays a very important role in the contribution of strength.

Grain boundary strengthening effect Δσ gb means that by reducing the grain size of the alloy, the superficial area of grain boundaries can increase, so the slip of dislocations is limited to the narrower grains and plugged at the grain boundaries and then increases the slip resistance of the dislocations.

The dislocation strengthening effect Δσ dis is also called deformation strengthening or work hardening. According to the nature of dislocation strengthening, dislocations continue to proliferate after material deformation, and the dislocation density continues to increase, enhancing the interaction between dislocations.

The precipitation strengthening effect Δσor is also considered when establishing the strength model. A large number of needle-shaped precipitated phases are distributed within the matrix, which hinders the movement of the dislocation.
